findings.where: apps/web/lib/bank/match-opkey.ts:36-92 (MatchIntent / matchOpKeyFor) + apps/web/components/bank/matching-section.tsx:191-215 (setOutcome on the act() success callback) + packages/db/migrations/0004_governed_fns.sql:46-60 (_reserve_op)
findings.what: D15's 'one decision, one key' premise and AC4/AC10's promise of 'a current reread before any new intent' both fail for a legitimate, ordinary re-decision: match a line, unmatch it, then re-submit the IDENTICAL selection (same lines/entries/cents/ack). Because matchOpKeyFor is a PURE function of that tuple with no reference to the match's lifecycle, the second submission mints the SAME op_key as the first, and _reserve_op's idempotency check (same firm+fn+op_key, same request hash) returns the FIRST match's stored receipt WITHOUT re-running the door's actual matching logic at all. The face does not throw (matchBankLine only throws when match_id is absent), so the success callback fires and calls setOutcome(receipt) with the DEAD match's id/line_ids/entry_ids, rendering a persistent 'no new cash entry was created' block naming a match that the database has already recorded as `status='unmatched'`. The line remains genuinely unmatched (list_unmatched_lines still returns it, and the reloaded candidates/context confirm this), so the screen ends up self-contradictory: a green success card next to a line that visibly never left the unmatched report.
findings.evidence: INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED on clara_657 (throwaway node --test script against the real doors, deleted after the run; git status confirmed clean afterward, no tracked file touched). Sequence: draft+approve a 77,000-cent entry, enter a matching statement line, `matchBankLine(..., opKey: FIXED_KEY)` -> match id `4680003e-520b-4848-98f8-32699694d006`; `unmatchBankMatch(...)` -> `select status from clara.bank_matches` = `unmatched`; `list_unmatched_lines` shows the line again; resubmit the IDENTICAL intent under the SAME `FIXED_KEY`. Output: `second.match_id = 4680003e-... (same as first? true)`, `second.new_journal_entries = 0, settlement_objects = 0` (looks like a clean success), `live/pending members on the line after replay = 0`, `line STILL on unmatched report after the 'successful' resubmit = true`. Mechanism confirmed by source: `_reserve_op` (0004_governed_fns.sql:46-60) returns the STORED `result` whenever `(firm, fn, op_key)` already exists and the request hash agrees, with no re-execution and no epoch/lifecycle check; `matchOpKeyFor`'s `MatchIntent` (match-opkey.ts:36-46) carries only `{clientId, lineIds, entries, ackPeriodExceptions}` — nothing that changes when the referenced match is undone and redone. This is the same mechanism the adversarial-lens review already flagged as its own A1 blocker (reports/657-review-adversarial.json) with an independent live measurement; this review reproduces it from a cold rig state to confirm it is real and not an artifact of that session's fixtures. No cell in the delivered battery exercises this path: `p657.db.one-receipt-under-retry` only replays a key against its OWN first attempt (a lost-response retry), never a retry after an intervening `unmatch_bank_match`; the report's AC4/AC10 rows are marked 'done' on that narrower evidence.
findings.fix: Give the intent an epoch tied to the match lifecycle it is deciding about, not just the raw selection. Smallest fix that keeps D15's letter: fold the selected lines' CURRENT `match_id`/`group_status` (read off the context/candidate reads already on screen) into `MatchIntent` and `canonicalMatchIntent`, so a key renews the moment a referenced line's live match identity changes underneath it — add exactly the one clause the module's own renewal-rule comment (match-opkey.ts:5-10) is missing. Add the red cell described above (match -> unmatch -> resubmit the identical intent) to `bank-line-existing-booking.test.mjs` so it is asserted rather than merely reachable.

findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0226_bank_match_evidence.sql:568-627 (candidate_basis subselect) vs the same file's own header claim at §B (lines ~57-63) and §5's comment at lines ~517-522, 'one deterministic row per candidate entry of this line's bank account'
findings.what: The migration's own documented contract for `candidate_basis[]` is 'one row per CANDIDATE entry' — i.e. the same population `list_bank_match_candidates` returns. The actual query has no such filter: `list_bank_match_candidates` explicitly excludes entries with zero remaining capacity on either side (0226:350-351/474-475, `where (debit_remaining_cents)::bigint > 0 or (credit_remaining_cents)::bigint > 0`), but the `candidate_basis` subselect (0226:620-626) filters only on firm/client/approved/not-reversed/touches-the-COA — no remaining-capacity predicate at all. So `candidate_basis` is actually 'one row per approved bank-touching entry of the client', a strictly larger set than the candidates it claims to describe, and it runs two extra correlated capacity aggregates per row with no bound on the client's approved bank history.
findings.evidence: Source-confirmed by direct comparison of the two subselects in the same file (list_bank_match_candidates: 0226:344-351; candidate_basis: 0226:619-627). No face-visible symptom TODAY only because `matching-candidates.tsx`'s `basisFor` map is built from `candidate_basis` but looked up BY the candidate list's own entry ids (an accident of the join, not a guard) — a fully-spent entry's basis row is computed and shipped over the wire but never rendered. This matches the adversarial-lens review's independently-measured A2 finding (reports/657-review-adversarial.json), which counted 3 basis rows against 2 real candidates on a seeded fixture; this review corroborates it from the source side (the missing predicate is unambiguous by inspection) rather than re-running that live cell.
findings.fix: Apply the same capacity predicate the candidate read applies: compute the side-relevant remaining-capacity value once (it already exists inside the `amount_exact` CASE), lift it to a named column, and filter the outer `jsonb_agg` on it the way 0226:349-351 does. That makes the header's own sentence true, bounds the payload to the population it claims to describe, and removes an unbounded per-click cost from `get_bank_line_matching_context`.
